title: HTTP Schema Resource
description: An HTTP Schema Resource describes the HTTP methods of a Semantic HTTP Resource that the resource supports, and may describe more. It is an OpenAPI 3.1 Path Item Object with extra constraints: every request and response media type links to a schema and, unless the media type carries RDF in-band, to an RDF context.

AbsoluteUri.description: An absolute URI: a URI with a scheme, not a relative reference. It may have a fragment. It contains no space and none of the characters < > " { } | \ ^ `, which a URI cannot contain.

PathItem.description: The methods of a Semantic HTTP Resource that the resource supports, and possibly more. Only the OpenAPI Path Item fields listed here are allowed, plus x- extensions. A $ref Path Item is not allowed. An x- extension key MUST NOT contain a colon, because JSON-LD reads such a key as an IRI.

Operation.description: An HTTP method that the resource supports. It MUST list its responses. Only the OpenAPI 3.1 Operation fields listed here are allowed, plus x- extensions, as in Request Body, Response and Media Type: JSON-LD would lift some other keys, such as @context, an IRI or a context term. Neither an Operation-level servers field nor a $ref member is allowed, so it cannot be a Reference Object. An x- extension key MUST NOT contain a colon, because JSON-LD reads such a key as an IRI.

RequestBody.description: The content a client may send with the method. It MUST list its media types. Only the OpenAPI 3.1 Request Body fields listed here are allowed, plus x- extensions. A $ref member is not allowed, so it cannot be a Reference Object. An x- extension key MUST NOT contain a colon, because JSON-LD reads such a key as an IRI.

Responses.description: Responses keyed by a three digit status code, a range such as 2XX, or default. There MUST be at least one key and every key MUST be one of these; x- extension keys are not allowed, because the RDF context reads every key as a status code.

Response.description: A response the method may return. Only the OpenAPI 3.1 Response fields listed here are allowed, plus x- extensions. A $ref member is not allowed, so it cannot be a Reference Object. An x- extension key MUST NOT contain a colon, because JSON-LD reads such a key as an IRI.

Content.description: Media types keyed by media type. The type and subtype of every key MUST be lowercase; parameters after the first ; may have any case. The six RDF media types that carry RDF in-band (with optional parameters) MUST NOT have an x-rdf-context; every other media type MUST have one.

MediaType.description: A media type with exactly one of schema or x-schema, and an x-rdf-context where Content requires one. Only the OpenAPI 3.1 Media Type fields listed here are allowed, plus x- extensions. A $ref member is not allowed on the media type itself, so it cannot be a Reference Object; a JSON Schema is referenced by the $ref inside schema. An x- extension key MUST NOT contain a colon, because JSON-LD reads such a key as an IRI.

schema.description: A reference to an external schema, as a $ref to an absolute URI, which may have a fragment. Inline schemas are not allowed.

x-schema.description: A link to a schema that is not a JSON Schema, such as an XML Schema.

x-rdf-context.description: A link to the RDF context that gives the content its RDF meaning.

LinkTarget.description: A link to a document: its absolute URI, which may have a fragment, and its media type, and no other members.
